title: Viradha
hook: a roar in the deep forest, and something huge snatches Sita before anyone can draw a bow

segments.voice: Yesterday: the last soft place. The sages hosted Rama with water, a seat and food, and at sunrise he walked into the deep forest.

The noise comes first: a roar that shakes the trees. Then the shape, tall as a hill, with a gaping mouth and a huge iron spear, and on the spear, Valmiki says, hang the animals he has killed, lions, tigers and deer. His name is Viradha. Before Rama or Lakshmana can move, he grabs Sita, lifts her, and steps back, holding her. Then he speaks, and laughs at them.
screen: `A ROAR THAT SHAKES THE TREES.` → `A SPEAR HUNG WITH ANIMALS.` → `HE GRABS SITA.`

segments.voice: Viradha mocks them. You look like ascetics, with your bark and matted hair, but you carry bows and you have a woman with you. What kind of hermits are you? She'll be my wife now. And he adds: Brahma gave me a boon. No weapon can kill me. Rama's first response is grief. He turns to Lakshmana, stricken: seeing Sita in a stranger's grip hurts more than his father's death, more than losing the kingdom. It's Lakshmana, furious, who pulls him back into the moment. Both brothers shoot. Arrows strike Viradha again and again and don't kill him. He drops Sita, seizes the two brothers, swings them onto his shoulders like children, and runs off into the forest, Sita screaming after them. And the brothers, carried along, do the only thing left. They break his arms, Rama the right, Lakshmana the left. Viradha falls. So the week ends. Bharata suspected on the road. Sandals stepped into on Chitrakoot. A throne at Nandigrama with no king on it, and Anasuya's gifts. Sages asking for a protector, the heat of tapas, a guest welcomed as a god. And today the welcome ends, and the forest shows its teeth.
screen: `WHAT KIND OF HERMITS ARE YOU?` · `NO WEAPON CAN KILL ME.` · `CARRIED OFF ON HIS SHOULDERS.` · `THE WEEK, FROM THE TOP.` · then, large: `THE FOREST SHOWS ITS TEETH.`

segments.voice: Think of a moment when something sudden happened, a shock, a bad phone call, a near miss, and you froze; let the memory be there without replaying it, and send a slow breath to wherever your body tightened. Rama froze in grief and his brother called him back, so imagine someone you trust saying your name, steady, calling you back into the room.
Viradha. The forest giant who seizes Sita, mocks the brothers as false hermits, and can't be killed by weapons.
Your line: no weapon can kill me. The forest has set its first test. See you tomorrow.

screen: `DAY 553 COUNTS.` → `A WEEK FROM CHITRAKOOT INTO THE WILD, DONE.` → `TOMORROW: VIRADHA, PART TWO.`

howItsDone: Viradha is the first danger Rama meets in the Aranya Kanda, and reciters linger on Rama's grief when Sita is seized.

original.note: Sanskrit virādha: the name of the forest giant Rama meets first in the Aranya Kanda.

trapdoor: what you thought: Viradha is just a monster in the woods.
what it means: he's protected by a boon, and he mocks Rama's whole way of life.
what a scholar hears: Aranya 2–4 make Viradha the forest's first test, and some readers hear his question, why do hermits carry bows, again later in Sita's own words.

chat.says: Why couldn't Rama and Lakshmana just shoot Viradha with arrows?
options: A boon from Brahma meant no weapon could kill him, so the arrows failed.
His skin was too thick, so the arrows bounced off without harming him.
They didn't want to hurt him, because he was holding Sita at the time.
chat.meaning: Viradha had a boon from Brahma: no weapon could kill him. The arrows struck but failed, so the brothers broke his arms.

Viradha.meaning: a forest giant protected from weapons by a boon

Brahma.meaning: the creator god, who grants boons

Nandigrama.meaning: the village outside Ayodhya where Bharata ruled

Anasuya.meaning: Atri's wife, an ascetic famous for her austerity

sources.ref: Valmiki Ramayana, Aranya Kanda 2–4 (Viradha seizes Sita; the boon; the fight; the broken arms)
